nodes.content: Develop a semantic parser that generalizes variable binding and quantifier scope to unseen compositions without sacrificing familiar-construction accuracy.
requirements: Achieve ≥90% logical-form exact match on withheld scope–binding combinations with matched vocabulary and length distributions.
Keep familiar-construction exact-match accuracy within two percentage points of an equally sized supervised baseline.

nodes.content: Train ScopeBind to decode alpha-normalized logical forms via binder-link and scope-permutation actions, using counterfactual recombination plus familiar-example rehearsal.
How should ScopeBind filter counterfactual recombinations that violate binder accessibility under nested quantifier scopes?
Filtering recombinations by scope-tree dominance and binder-type compatibility will achieve ≥90% withheld exact match without exceeding a two-point familiar-accuracy deficit.
Generate ScopeBind recombinations; filter by scope-tree dominance and binder type; compare withheld and familiar exact match against supervised baseline.
Run three-seed ScopeBind ablations on matched withheld/familiar splits, comparing dominance/type-filtered recombination against unfiltered and supervised baselines by exact match.
Across three seeds, filtered ScopeBind reached 91.8% withheld exact match versus 76.4% unfiltered; familiar accuracy was 94.1% versus 95.3% supervised.
Ablate dominance and binder-type filters separately; audit 200 nested-scope examples for accessibility errors and measure withheld/familiar exact match.
On an independent vocabulary/length-matched withheld scope–binding split, filtered ScopeBind scored 86% exact match; 23/200 audited cases violated accessibility.
Can scope-state-constrained decoding eliminate the 23/200 audited accessibility violations without exceeding the two-point familiar-accuracy margin?
Scope-state decoding atop filtered ScopeBind should yield ≥90% withheld exact match and ≤2/200 accessibility errors, with ≤2-point familiar deficit.
Implement a scope-state decoder masking inaccessible binder links, then rerun matched-split exact-match tests and the 200-case accessibility audit.
Implement scope-stack binder masking in ScopeBind; rerun three-seed independent withheld/familiar exact-match tests and the 200-case accessibility audit.
Scope-stack masking yielded 1/200 accessibility errors and 94.0% familiar exact match, but only 88.7% independent withheld exact match.
Are residual withheld errors driven by incorrect quantifier ordering rather than binder accessibility after scope-stack masking?
Adding quantifier-order ranking to scope-state ScopeBind should reach ≥90% withheld exact match, ≤2/200 accessibility errors, and ≤2-point familiar deficit.
Classify residual withheld errors, train a quantifier-order reranker over scope-valid candidates, and rerun matched-split exact match and accessibility audits.
Classify errors from the 88.7% withheld run; train a scope-valid quantifier-order reranker and measure exact match and accessibility.
Quantifier-order errors comprised 68/100 audited residual cases; reranking reached 91.2% withheld, 94.0% familiar exact match, and 1/200 accessibility errors.
Adopt scope-state ScopeBind with quantifier-order reranking: 91.2% withheld exact match and a 1.3-point familiar deficit meet both targets.
Audit 100 residual errors from adopted ScopeBind on the independent withheld split, classifying quantifier-order, binder-link, and lexical mistakes.
ScopeBind Residual-100 audit sheet with gold and predicted logical forms, labeling 100 withheld failures by quantifier-order, binder-link, or lexical error.
Build a typed CCG chart parser enumerating binding-safe scope derivations, with a neural ranker trained on recombinations and familiar examples.
Does a 64-derivation-per-cell typed CCG chart cover ≥95% of gold withheld logical forms?
A 64-derivation-per-cell typed CCG chart will include ≥95% of gold withheld logical forms while preserving familiar derivations.
Measure gold-form chart coverage and neural-ranker exact match for 64-beam typed CCG on matched withheld/familiar splits versus supervised baseline.
Typed CCG chart covered 97.1% of withheld gold forms; ranker achieved 90.6% withheld and 94.2% familiar exact match (95.3% baseline).
Retrieve familiar quantifier and binding fragments, unify typed argument slots into novel scope graphs, then rerank compiled logical forms.
Index typed fragments, unify accessible binder slots, rerank compiled forms, and compare matched withheld/familiar exact match against the supervised baseline.
Independently validate Residual-100 error labels, then benchmark typed-fragment unification on withheld and familiar splits by error class and exact match.
Typed-fragment unification scored 87.9% withheld and 94.4% familiar exact match; 41/100 Residual-100 cases lacked compatible scope fragments.
Reject typed-fragment unification as the primary parser: 87.9% withheld exact match misses 90%, and 41/100 failures lack compatible fragments.
Train a variable-free continuation parser with typed composition and familiar-example rehearsal; deterministically compile programs into alpha-normalized logical forms.
Can variable-free continuation programs represent every withheld scope–binding gold form without collapsing distinct quantifier readings?
Typed continuation programs will compile ≥99% of withheld gold forms and preserve distinct logical forms for ≥99% of scope-contrast pairs.
Convert withheld gold forms to typed continuation programs; measure round-trip alpha-normalized exact match and scope-contrast preservation.
Convert withheld gold forms to typed continuations, train rehearsed decoder, and measure round-trip coverage, contrast preservation, and splitwise exact match.
Typed continuations round-tripped 99.6% of withheld forms, preserved 99.2% of scope contrasts, and achieved 90.4%/94.0% withheld/familiar exact match.
Recheck withheld round-trip coverage by nesting depth and compile 300 scope-contrast pairs, scoring distinct alpha-normalized logical forms.
On 300 independent scope-contrast pairs, only 294 (98.0%) compiled distinctly; depth-three withheld forms round-tripped at 96.8%.
Do the six collapsed scope contrasts arise from missing quantifier-order annotations in depth-three continuation programs?
Adding explicit quantifier-order tags to depth-three continuations will separate all six collapsed contrasts and raise round-trip coverage to ≥99%.
Annotate depth-three continuations with quantifier-order tags, recompile six collapsed contrasts, and measure depth-three round-trip coverage.
Tag depth-three continuations and retrain the decoder; retest six collapsed contrasts and coverage, comparing accuracy against 90.4%/94.0% withheld/familiar.
Quantifier-order tags separated all six contrasts and raised depth-three round-trip coverage from 96.8% to 99.3%; withheld/familiar exact match was 90.8%/94.1%.
Adopt tagged continuations over untagged: all six collapsed contrasts resolve, and withheld/familiar exact match rises from 90.4%/94.0% to 90.8%/94.1%.
Ablate quantifier-order tags in the adopted continuation parser; inspect six formerly collapsed contrasts and 100 depth-three pairs for scope collisions.
ScopeTag Ablation Report: tag-on/off logical forms for six formerly collapsed contrasts and 100 depth-three pairs, with scope-collision labels.
Cross-check ScopeTag collision labels against Residual-100 categories, then rerun tagged continuations on audited failures to quantify recovered exact matches.
Cross-check identified 19/100 Residual-100 failures with ScopeTag collision signatures; tagged continuations recovered 12/19 exact forms.
Select ScopeBind (91.2%) as primary, tagged continuations for collision fallback (12/19 recoveries); retain CCG comparator, reject subthreshold fragments.
